contents.title: Environment Setup, NestJS Core, and Dependency Injection
contents.description: Set up a professional Node.js environment, install NestJS via CLI, build a production-ready folder structure, and master Dependency Injection together with the Module system.
contents.body:
## I. Introduction

Many developers starting a backend project think installing **Node.js**, creating an `index.js`, and calling a few **Express** functions is enough. That mindset works for small prototypes, but once the project grows to dozens of modules and hundreds of APIs, everything quickly becomes messy: tangled imports, manual `new` object creation everywhere, and poor testability or replaceability without touching many files.

**NestJS** was created to solve exactly this problem. Instead of forcing developers to invent architecture from scratch, the framework provides a **Module** architecture, **Dependency Injection (DI)**, and powerful code generation via **CLI**. This lesson takes you from environment setup to understanding how NestJS manages the lifecycle of application components.

## II. Essence

This lesson follows a **code-first** approach: read the source first, then run APIs to validate the flow ***Controller -> Service -> Cross-module Service***.

Clone [here](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/system-design-mastery/introduction-to-kubernetes)

### Runtime Dependency Diagram

```mermaid
graph LR
    Client((Client))
    Client --> DogController[DogController]
    DogController --> DogService[DogService]
    DogService --> CatService["CatService - exported from CatModule"]
```

### Source Code Tree (File Level)

```mermaid
treeView-beta
    "src"
        "app.module.ts"
        "modules"
            "cat"
                "cat.module.ts"
                "cat.controller.ts"
                "cat.service.ts"
            "dog"
                "dog.module.ts"
                "dog.controller.ts"
                "dog.service.ts"
```

### Environment Setup and Run Flow

- **1. Prerequisites:** Install **Node.js LTS** (recommended v18+), and **npm**/**pnpm**. If Nest CLI is not installed, add `@nestjs/cli`.
- **2. Clone the demo source:** Clone/pull the source for the correct context:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/fullstack-mastery/environment-setup-and-nestjs-core
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Install dependencies:** In the project folder, install packages:
  ```bash
  npm install
  ```
- **4. Run command:** Start the app in dev mode:
  ```bash
  npm run start:dev
  ```
- **5. Success signal:** Terminal shows the app running on port `3000`; `GET /cats` returns valid JSON.

### Application Testing

- **Step 1:** Smoke-test the basic endpoint `GET /cats` to confirm successful boot:
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats
  ```
  *Expected result:* The response returns a cat list (or sample data) with HTTP `200`.

  *Conclusion:* The environment runs successfully, and the controller/service in `CatModule` works.

- **Step 2:** Verify cross-module DI via `GET /dogs/spy`:

  **API Title:** **Dog API - spy cat data - GET http://localhost:3000/dogs/spy**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send a `GET` request to `http://localhost:3000/dogs/spy`.

  **JSON Body:** No body for `GET`.

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3000/dogs/spy
  ```

  **Trace code execution (by file):**
  - [`src/modules/dog/dog.controller.ts:36`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/environment-setup-and-nestjs-core/src/modules/dog/dog.controller.ts#L36) -> `DogController.spyOnCat()`
  - [`src/modules/dog/dog.service.ts:55`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/environment-setup-and-nestjs-core/src/modules/dog/dog.service.ts#L55) -> `DogService.spyOnCat()`
  - [`src/modules/cat/cat.service.ts:76`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/environment-setup-and-nestjs-core/src/modules/cat/cat.service.ts#L76) -> `CatService.introduce()`
  - [`src/modules/cat/cat.module.ts:1`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/environment-setup-and-nestjs-core/src/modules/cat/cat.module.ts#L1) -> export `CatService`
  - [`src/modules/dog/dog.module.ts:1`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/environment-setup-and-nestjs-core/src/modules/dog/dog.module.ts#L1) -> import `CatModule`

  ```ts
  // Phase 1 - Trace paragraph 1
  // src/modules/dog/dog.controller.ts:36
  // Phase 1 - Router matches endpoint at DogController
  @Get('spy')
  spyOnCat() {
    // Phase 2 - Delegate business logic to DogService
    return this.dogService.spyOnCat();
  }

  // Phase 2 - Trace paragraph 2
  // src/modules/dog/dog.service.ts:55
  // Phase 3 - DogService calls CatService (provider from another module)
  spyOnCat() {
    const catIntro = this.catService.introduce();
    return `Dog says: "I overheard my neighbor say: '${catIntro}'"`;
  }

  // Phase 3 - Trace paragraph 3
  // src/modules/cat/cat.service.ts:76
  introduce() {
    return '🐱 Hello! I am a Cat. I am managed by the NestJS IoC Container.';
  }
  ```

  *Expected result:* Response data comes from `DogService` and proves `DogService` can call `CatService`.

  *Conclusion:* The `Controller -> Service -> Cross-module Service` flow works when the source module exports the provider and the destination module imports the module correctly.

## III. Core Concepts

### 1. ***Dependency Injection (DI)***

- **Role:** Separates object creation from business logic; classes only declare dependencies via constructor.
- **Common mistake:** Forgetting to register a provider in `providers` or forgetting to `export` a provider for cross-module use.
- **Production impact:** App fails at bootstrap or throws runtime errors because dependencies cannot be resolved.

### 2. ***Module Encapsulation***

- **Role:** `@Module()` creates business boundaries; providers are private by default.
- **Common mistake:** Importing a module without exporting the required provider in the source module.
- **Production impact:** Teams duplicate code or create circular dependencies, making architecture hard to maintain.

### 3. ***Singleton Provider***

- **Role:** NestJS creates one provider instance for the whole app by default, reducing object creation cost.
- **Common mistake:** Storing mutable state in singletons without concurrency control.
- **Production impact:** Data can be overwritten across requests, causing hard-to-reproduce bugs.

### 4. ***NestJS CLI and File-Level Structure***

- **Role:** Standardizes project skeleton (`main.ts`, `app.module.ts`, feature modules) to accelerate onboarding.
- **Common mistake:** Putting all controllers/services into one bloated folder instead of domain modules.
- **Production impact:** Hard team scaling, frequent merge conflicts, and unclear domain-based tests.

## IV. Advanced Techniques

**NestJS** is not only an HTTP framework; it is a complete architectural ecosystem. From environment standardization with **nvm** and **CLI**, to **Feature Module** organization, to delegating object creation to the **IoC Container** through **Dependency Injection**, everything points to one goal: maintainable, testable, and scalable code.

The **Module** system, with encapsulation and export/import mechanics, is the backbone of every NestJS project. Understanding how modules communicate through DI is the first step to building a robust backend architecture.

**Conclusion:** Do not write code first and think about architecture later. Let **NestJS** enforce structure from your first line, and your project can scale without losing control.

## V. Interview Questions

1. **Interview Question:**  
   "In this lesson, why can `DogService` call `CatService` without `new CatService()`?"
   - **What is being assessed:** Correct understanding of **DI**, module `imports`/`exports`, and the IoC Container role.
   - **Expected answer direction:** `CatModule` must `export CatService`, and `DogModule` must `import CatModule`; NestJS resolves dependencies through constructor injection.

2. **Interview Question:**  
   "If you remove `imports: [CatModule]` from `DogModule`, what runtime issue happens to `GET /dogs/spy`?"
   - **What is being assessed:** Ability to read dependency resolution errors and isolate issues by module boundary.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Mention the error like *Nest can't resolve dependencies of the DogService* and explain that the provider is unavailable in that module context.

3. **Interview Question:**  
   "As the codebase grows across many domains, how would you organize modules and services to reduce coupling and keep testability?"
   - **What is being assessed:** Backend design thinking with `module-by-feature`, controller/service separation, and team scalability.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Split by domain, export only shared providers, avoid circular dependencies, and prefer constructor injection for easier mocking/testing.

  ```ts
  }

  // src/modules/cat/cat.service.ts:76
  introduce() {
    return '🐱 Hello! I am a Cat. I am managed by the NestJS IoC Container.';
  }
  ```

  *Kết quả mong đợi:* Response trả dữ liệu từ `DogService` và thể hiện `DogService` gọi được `CatService`.

  *Kết luận:* Luồng `Controller -> Service -> Cross-module Service` hoạt động khi module nguồn export provider và module đích import module đúng cách.

## III. Các khái niệm cốt lõi

### 1. ***Dependency Injection (DI)***

- **Vai trò:** Tách khâu khởi tạo object khỏi business logic; class chỉ khai báo dependency qua constructor.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Quên đăng ký provider trong `providers` hoặc quên `export` provider cần dùng chéo module.
- **Hậu quả production:** App fail khi bootstrap hoặc phát sinh lỗi runtime do không resolve được dependency.

### 2. ***Module Encapsulation***

- **Vai trò:** `@Module()` tạo ranh giới nghiệp vụ; provider mặc định private trong module.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Import module nhưng không export provider tương ứng ở module nguồn.
- **Hậu quả production:** Team phải duplicate code hoặc tạo dependency vòng, kiến trúc khó bảo trì.

### 3. ***Singleton Provider***

- **Vai trò:** NestJS mặc định tạo một instance/provider cho toàn app, giảm chi phí tạo object.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Đặt mutable state trong singleton mà không kiểm soát cạnh tranh dữ liệu.
- **Hậu quả production:** Data bị ghi đè giữa request, gây bug khó tái hiện.

### 4. ***NestJS CLI và cấu trúc file-level***

- **Vai trò:** Chuẩn hoá skeleton dự án (`main.ts`, `app.module.ts`, module theo feature) để tăng tốc onboarding.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Để toàn bộ controller/service trong một thư mục phình to, không tách module theo domain.
- **Hậu quả production:** Khó mở rộng theo team, conflict merge cao, test theo domain kém rõ ràng.

## IV. Kỹ thuật nâng cao

**NestJS** không chỉ là một framework HTTP mà là một hệ sinh thái kiến trúc hoàn chỉnh. Từ việc chuẩn hoá môi trường với **nvm** và **CLI**, tổ chức thư mục theo **Feature Module**, đến việc uỷ thác toàn bộ việc khởi tạo object cho **IoC Container** thông qua **Dependency Injection**, mọi thứ đều hướng tới một mục tiêu: code dễ mở rộng, dễ test, và dễ bảo trì.

Hệ thống **Module** với cơ chế đóng gói (encapsulation) và export/import là xương sống của mọi dự án NestJS. Hiểu rõ cách các module giao tiếp với nhau thông qua DI chính là bước đầu tiên để xây dựng kiến trúc backend vững chắc.

**Kết luận:** Đừng viết code rồi mới nghĩ kiến trúc. Hãy để **NestJS** ép bạn vào khuôn khổ ngay từ dòng đầu tiên, và bạn sẽ thấy dự án lớn dần mà không bao giờ mất kiểm soát.

## V. Các mẫu câu phỏng vấn

1. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   “Trong bài này, vì sao `DogService` có thể gọi được `CatService` mà không cần `new CatService()`?”
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Ứng viên có hiểu đúng cơ chế **DI**, `imports`/`exports` giữa module và vai trò của IoC Container.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Nêu được `CatModule` phải `export CatService`, `DogModule` phải `import CatModule`; NestJS tự resolve dependency qua constructor injection.

2. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   “Nếu bỏ `imports: [CatModule]` khỏi `DogModule`, endpoint `GET /dogs/spy` sẽ gặp vấn đề gì trên runtime?”
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Khả năng đọc lỗi dependency resolution và khoanh vùng lỗi theo module boundary.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Nêu đúng lỗi kiểu *Nest can't resolve dependencies of the DogService*; giải thích nguyên nhân là provider không available trong module context.

3. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   “Khi codebase lớn dần theo nhiều domain, bạn tổ chức module và service thế nào để giảm coupling và giữ testability?”
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Tư duy thiết kế backend theo `module-by-feature`, tách trách nhiệm controller/service, và khả năng mở rộng team.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Đề cập chia module theo domain, chỉ export provider cần chia sẻ, tránh phụ thuộc vòng, ưu tiên constructor injection để dễ mock/test.
Thiết lập Môi trường, NestJS Core & Dependency Injection
Set up a professional Node.js environment, install NestJS via CLI, build a production-ready folder structure, and master Dependency Injection together with the Module system.
Environment Setup, NestJS Core, and Dependency Injection
Khởi tạo môi trường Node.js chuyên nghiệp, cài đặt NestJS qua CLI, xây dựng cấu trúc thư mục chuẩn production, và nắm vững Dependency Injection cùng hệ thống Module.

challenges.requirements: Create a ***NestJS*** project using the CLI with folder name `order-inventory-cross-module-di`. Build an `InventoryModule` (containing `InventoryService`) and an `OrderModule` (containing `OrderController` + `OrderService`). `InventoryModule` must `export` `InventoryService`; `OrderModule` must `import` `InventoryModule`; `OrderService` must inject `InventoryService` through its constructor - **forbidden** to use `new InventoryService()` or global singletons. contents.title: HTTP Request Lifecycle
contents.description: Understand the exact journey of an HTTP packet through Middleware, Guard, Interceptor, and Pipe before it reaches the Controller, and how NestJS standardizes responses on the way out.
contents.body:
## I. Introduction
In simple frameworks like ***Express***, requests go directly to handlers, so auth, validation, and response formatting often get mixed in one place. As routes increase, controllers become bloated, harder to debug, and harder to test.

***NestJS*** separates requests into a pipeline with a clear execution order. This is essential for production backend work: put authorization in ***Guards***, validation in ***Pipes***, and response normalization in ***Interceptors***.

## II. Essence
This lesson follows a **code-first** approach: read the real pipeline source first, then test APIs to clearly see the order `Middleware -> Guard -> Interceptor -> Pipe -> Controller -> Service`.

Clone [here](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/system-design-mastery/introduction-to-kubernetes)

### Runtime Dependency Diagram

```mermaid
graph LR
    Client((Client)) --> ReqId[RequestIdMiddleware]
    ReqId --> Logger[LoggerMiddleware]
    Logger --> Guard[TimingGuard]
    Guard --> IntIn[ExecutionTimerInterceptor]
    IntIn --> IntWrap[ResponseTransformInterceptor]
    IntWrap --> Pipe[ParsePositiveIntPipe]
    Pipe --> Ctrl[ItemsController]
    Ctrl --> Svc[ItemsService]
    Svc --> IntWrap
```

### Source Code Tree (File Level)

```mermaid
treeView-beta
    "src"
        "main.ts"
        "app.module.ts"
        "common"
            "middleware"
                "request-id.middleware.ts"
                "logger.middleware.ts"
            "guards"
                "timing.guard.ts"
            "interceptors"
                "execution-timer.interceptor.ts"
                "response-transform.interceptor.ts"
            "pipes"
                "parse-positive-int.pipe.ts"
        "modules"
            "items"
                "items.controller.ts"
                "items.service.ts"
                "dto/create-item.dto.ts"
```

### Environment Setup and Run Flow

- **1. Prerequisites:** Require `Node.js LTS`, `npm`, and git.
- **2. Clone source demo:** Clone/pull the source to work with the correct code context:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/fullstack-mastery/request-lifecycle
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Install dependencies:** Install packages in the project directory:
  ```bash
  npm install
  ```
- **4. Run command:** Start the app locally:
  ```bash
  npm run start:dev
  ```
- **5. Success signal:** Server starts on port `3000`, and `GET /items` returns the standardized response wrapper.

### Application Testing

- **Step 1:** Smoke-test endpoint `GET /items`:
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3000/items
  ```
  *Expected result:* Response follows the standard format `{ data, timestamp, requestId }` with HTTP `200`.

  **Sample response (example):**
  ```json
  {
    "data": [
      { "id": 1, "name": "Laptop", "description": "A powerful laptop" }
    ],
    "timestamp": "2026-04-20T10:30:00.000Z",
    "requestId": "2b9f0f15-2f34-4ea1-b77e-8c55f66a2a2e"
  }
  ```

  *Conclusion:* `ResponseTransformInterceptor` successfully wraps output consistently for the whole system.

- **Step 2:** Test the full `GET /items/:id` flow with a Pipe:

  **API Title:** **Items API - get by id - GET http://localhost:3000/items/5**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send `GET` to `http://localhost:3000/items/5`.

  **JSON Body:** No body for `GET`.

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3000/items/5
  ```

  **Trace code execution (by file):**
  - [`src/common/middleware/request-id.middleware.ts:27`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/request-lifecycle/src/common/middleware/request-id.middleware.ts#L27) -> `RequestIdMiddleware.use()`
  - [`src/common/guards/timing.guard.ts:38`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/request-lifecycle/src/common/guards/timing.guard.ts#L38) -> `TimingGuard.canActivate()`
  - [`src/common/pipes/parse-positive-int.pipe.ts:31`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/request-lifecycle/src/common/pipes/parse-positive-int.pipe.ts#L31) -> `ParsePositiveIntPipe.transform()`
  - [`src/modules/items/items.controller.ts:76`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/request-lifecycle/src/modules/items/items.controller.ts#L76) -> `ItemsController.findOne()`
  - [`src/modules/items/items.service.ts:55`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/request-lifecycle/src/modules/items/items.service.ts#L55) -> `ItemsService.findOne()`

  ```ts
  // Phase 1 - Trace paragraph 1
  // src/common/middleware/request-id.middleware.ts
  use(req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): void {
    const requestId = (req.headers['x-request-id'] as string) ?? uuidv4();
    req.headers['x-request-id'] = requestId;
    res.setHeader('x-request-id', requestId);
    next();
  }

  // Phase 2 - Trace paragraph 2
  // src/common/guards/timing.guard.ts
  canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): boolean {
    const request = context.switchToHttp().getRequest<Request>();
    const guardEntryTime = Date.now();
    request.headers['x-guard-entry-time'] = String(guardEntryTime);
    return true;
  }

  // Phase 3 - Trace paragraph 3
  // src/common/pipes/parse-positive-int.pipe.ts
  transform(value: string, metadata: ArgumentMetadata): number {
    const parsed = parseInt(value, 10);
    if (isNaN(parsed)) {
      throw new BadRequestException(
        `Validation failed for param '${metadata.data}': '${value}' is not a number`,
      );
    }
    if (parsed <= 0) {
      throw new BadRequestException(
        `Validation failed for param '${metadata.data}': ${parsed} must be a positive integer (> 0)`,
      );
    }
    return parsed;
  }

  // Phase 4 - Trace paragraph 4
  // src/modules/items/items.controller.ts
  @Get(':id')
  findOne(@Param('id', ParsePositiveIntPipe) id: number): Item {
    // Phase 1 - Handler calls service after id passes Pipe
    return this.itemsService.findOne(id);
  }

  // Phase 5 - Trace paragraph 5
  // src/modules/items/items.service.ts
  findOne(id: number): Item {
    // Phase 2 - Business lookup in service
    const item = this.items.find((i) => i.id === id);
    if (!item) {
      throw new Error(`Item with id ${id} not found`);
    }
    return item;
  }
  ```

  *Expected result:* A valid request returns the correct item by id, with `timestamp` + `requestId` in the response wrapper.

  *Conclusion:* Keeping validation in Pipe ensures controller/service only process clean data.

## III. Core Concepts

### 1. ***Middleware***

- **Role:** Attach metadata (`x-request-id`) and log requests before entering deeper pipeline stages.
- **Common mistake:** Forgetting `next()`, causing requests to hang.
- **Production impact:** Lose request-id tracing capability, making cross-service debugging difficult.

### 2. ***Guard***

- **Role:** Decide whether a request can continue and optionally attach entry timestamp.
- **Common mistake:** Putting auth logic inside controller instead of guard.
- **Production impact:** Inconsistent policies across routes and higher bypass risk.

### 3. ***Pipe***

- **Role:** Validate/transform input before the handler executes.
- **Common mistake:** Validating too late in the service layer.
- **Production impact:** Wasted resources on invalid requests and unnecessary business errors.

### 4. ***Interceptor***

- **Role:** Wrap handlers to measure execution time and standardize response envelopes.
- **Common mistake:** Mixing business logic into interceptors.
- **Production impact:** Poor maintainability, weak separation of concerns, and harder latency debugging.

## IV. Advanced Techniques

The request lifecycle in **NestJS** is not abstract; it is a concrete layered architecture: **Middleware** -> **Guard** -> **Interceptor** -> **Pipe** -> **Controller** -> **Service** -> **Interceptor** (outbound) -> **Exception Filter**. Each layer solves a specific concern, and **NestJS** guarantees consistent execution order.

Understanding this pipeline helps developers place logic in the right layer: never validate in controllers, never format responses in services, and never enforce authorization in middleware.

**Conclusion:** Mastering request lifecycle means mastering how **NestJS** thinks. When every line of code lives in the right layer, the application naturally becomes cleaner, more testable, and easier to scale.

## V. Interview Questions

1. **Interview Question:**  
   â€œIn the NestJS request lifecycle, why should `ParsePositiveIntPipe` run before `ItemsController.findOne()`?â€
   - **What is being assessed:** Ability to separate validation from business logic and understand fail-fast design.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Pipe blocks bad input at the edge, reduces processing cost in controller/service, and returns consistent 400 errors.

2. **Interview Question:**  
   â€œIf you remove `ResponseTransformInterceptor`, how will the frontend be affected?â€
   - **What is being assessed:** API contract thinking and response consistency across endpoints.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Response shapes become inconsistent per route; frontend must handle many branches; tracing gets harder due to missing standard fields like `requestId`.

3. **Interview Question:**  
   â€œHow do Middleware, Guard, and Interceptor differ in a `GET /items/5` flow?â€
   - **What is being assessed:** Understanding of execution order and responsibilities for each pipeline layer.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Middleware enriches/logs requests; Guard authorizes/gates access; Interceptor wraps handlers to measure time and transform responses.

  *Conclusion:* Keeping validation in Pipe ensures controller/service only process clean data.

## III. Core Concepts

### 1. ***Middleware***

- **Role:** Attach metadata (`x-request-id`) and log requests before entering deeper pipeline stages.
- **Common mistake:** Forgetting `next()`, causing requests to hang.
- **Production impact:** Lose request-id tracing capability, making cross-service debugging difficult.

### 2. ***Guard***

- **Role:** Decide whether a request can continue and optionally attach entry timestamp.
- **Common mistake:** Putting auth logic inside controller instead of guard.
- **Production impact:** Inconsistent policies across routes and higher bypass risk.

### 3. ***Pipe***

- **Role:** Validate/transform input before the handler executes.
- **Common mistake:** Validating too late in the service layer.
- **Production impact:** Wasted resources on invalid requests and unnecessary business errors.

### 4. ***Interceptor***

- **Role:** Wrap handlers to measure execution time and standardize response envelopes.
- **Common mistake:** Mixing business logic into interceptors.
- **Production impact:** Poor maintainability, weak separation of concerns, and harder latency debugging.

## IV. Advanced Techniques

The request lifecycle in **NestJS** is not abstract; it is a concrete layered architecture: **Middleware** -> **Guard** -> **Interceptor** -> **Pipe** -> **Controller** -> **Service** -> **Interceptor** (outbound) -> **Exception Filter**. Each layer solves a specific concern, and **NestJS** guarantees consistent execution order.

Understanding this pipeline helps developers place logic in the right layer: never validate in controllers, never format responses in services, and never enforce authorization in middleware.

**Conclusion:** Mastering request lifecycle means mastering how **NestJS** thinks. When every line of code lives in the right layer, the application naturally becomes cleaner, more testable, and easier to scale.

## V. Interview Questions

1. **Interview Question:**  
   â€œIn the NestJS request lifecycle, why should `ParsePositiveIntPipe` run before `ItemsController.findOne()`?â€
   - **What is being assessed:** Ability to separate validation from business logic and understand fail-fast design.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Pipe blocks bad input at the edge, reduces processing cost in controller/service, and returns consistent 400 errors.

2. **Interview Question:**  
   â€œIf you remove `ResponseTransformInterceptor`, how will the frontend be affected?â€
   - **What is being assessed:** API contract thinking and response consistency across endpoints.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Response shapes become inconsistent per route; frontend must handle many branches; tracing gets harder due to missing standard fields like `requestId`.

3. **Interview Question:**  
   â€œHow do Middleware, Guard, and Interceptor differ in a `GET /items/5` flow?â€
   - **What is being assessed:** Understanding of execution order and responsibilities for each pipeline layer.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Middleware enriches/logs requests; Guard authorizes/gates access; Interceptor wraps handlers to measure time and transform responses.

## I. Lời mở đầu

Trong các framework đơn giản như ***Express***, request đi thẳng vào handler, khiến logic xác thực, validation và định dạng response thường bị trộn lẫn cùng một chỗ. Khi số lượng route tăng lên, controller trở nên cồng kềnh, khó debug và khó test.

***NestJS*** tách request thành một pipeline với thứ tự thực thi rõ ràng. Đây là yếu tố thiết yếu cho backend production: đặt authorization trong ***Guards***, validation trong ***Pipes***, và chuẩn hóa response trong ***Interceptors***.

## III. Các khái niệm cốt lõi

### 1. ***Middleware***

- **Vai trò:** Gắn metadata (`x-request-id`) và ghi log request trước khi đi vào các tầng sâu hơn trong pipeline.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Quên gọi `next()` khiến request bị treo vô thời hạn.
- **Hệ quả production:** Mất khả năng truy vết request-id, gỡ lỗi giữa các service trở nên rất khó.

### 2. ***Guard***

- **Vai trò:** Quyết định request có được tiếp tục hay không, và có thể gắn thêm metadata (timestamp, context).
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Nhồi logic auth vào ***Controller*** thay vì tách ra ***Guard***.
- **Hệ quả production:** Policy bảo mật không nhất quán giữa các route, rủi ro bị bypass tăng cao.

### 3. ***Pipe***

- **Vai trò:** Validate và transform dữ liệu đầu vào trước khi handler thực thi.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Validate quá muộn trong tầng ***Service***.
- **Hệ quả production:** Lãng phí tài nguyên xử lý request không hợp lệ, phát sinh lỗi business không cần thiết.

### 4. ***Interceptor***

- **Vai trò:** Bọc handler để đo thời gian thực thi và chuẩn hóa cấu trúc response.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Trộn business logic vào ***Interceptor***.
- **Hệ quả production:** Khó bảo trì, phân tách trách nhiệm yếu, debug latency khó hơn.

## IV. Kỹ thuật nâng cao

Vòng đời request trong ***NestJS*** không phải khái niệm trừu tượng mà là một kiến trúc phân tầng cụ thể: ***Middleware*** -> ***Guard*** -> ***Interceptor*** -> ***Pipe*** -> ***Controller*** -> ***Service*** -> ***Interceptor*** (outbound) -> ***Exception Filter***. Mỗi tầng giải quyết một mối quan tâm riêng biệt, và ***NestJS*** đảm bảo thứ tự thực thi nhất quán.

Hiểu rõ pipeline này giúp lập trình viên đặt logic đúng chỗ: không bao giờ validate trong ***Controller***, không bao giờ format response trong ***Service***, và không bao giờ kiểm tra quyền trong ***Middleware***.

**Kết luận:** Nắm vững vòng đời request là nắm vững cách ***NestJS*** tư duy. Khi mỗi dòng code nằm đúng tầng, ứng dụng tự nhiên trở nên dễ đọc hơn, dễ test hơn và dễ scale hơn.

## V. Các mẫu câu phỏng vấn

1. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   "Trong vòng đời request của NestJS, vì sao `ParsePositiveIntPipe` nên chạy trước `ItemsController.findOne()`?"
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Khả năng tách validation khỏi business logic và tư duy fail-fast.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** ***Pipe*** chặn input sai ngay tại biên, giảm chi phí xử lý trong ***Controller***/***Service*** và trả lỗi `400` nhất quán.

2. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   "Nếu bỏ `ResponseTransformInterceptor`, frontend sẽ bị ảnh hưởng thế nào?"
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Tư duy API contract và tính nhất quán response giữa các endpoint.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Cấu trúc response mỗi route mỗi khác; frontend phải xử lý nhiều nhánh; mất trường chuẩn như `requestId` khiến truy vết khó hơn.

3. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   "***Middleware***, ***Guard*** và ***Interceptor*** khác nhau thế nào trong luồng `GET /items/5`?"
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Hiểu thứ tự thực thi và trách nhiệm từng tầng pipeline.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** ***Middleware*** gắn metadata/log request; ***Guard*** kiểm soát quyền truy cập; ***Interceptor*** bọc handler để đo thời gian và transform response.

challenges.prerequisites:

challenges.description: Build a small NestJS project with a Book feature that travels through all 5 pipeline layers: Middleware -> Guard -> Pipe -> Controller -> Interceptor -> Exception Filter. Each layer lives in its own single file, registered at the correct scope (global / controller / method), and prints a log so the execution order is visible. Goal: watch one request traverse the pipeline and internalize which responsibility belongs to which layer.
challenges.requirements:
Create a ***NestJS*** project with folder name `book-pipeline-lifecycle`. Implement all 5 pipeline layers, each in **exactly one file**:
- `RequestIdMiddleware`: bound app-wide, generates `x-request-id` via `crypto.randomUUID()` if the client did not send one; attaches it onto `req` so downstream layers can read it.
- `ApiKeyGuard`: reads header `x-api-key`, compares against the constant `API_KEY = "dev-key-123"`; if missing/wrong -> throw `UnauthorizedException` with `code: "UNAUTHORIZED"`.
- `ParsePositiveIntPipe`: takes the `string` from `@Param('id')`, returns a positive integer `number`; parse failure or `<= 0` -> throw `BadRequestException` with `code: "INVALID_ID"`.
- `ResponseTransformInterceptor`: wraps every `2xx` response into `{data: <payload>, meta: {requestId, timestamp}}`.
- `AllExceptionsFilter`: catches every exception, returns `{code, message}`; sets header `x-request-id` on the error path too.

Business feature: `BookController` exposes exactly one endpoint `GET /books/:id` returning `{id, title}` with `title` = `"Book ${id}"` (mock).

**Forbidden:** validating `id` inside the controller with `if`; checking auth/role inside middleware; putting two layers in one file.

challenges.title: CRUD Article with JwtAuthGuard, RolesGuard, custom Pipe and LoggingInterceptor
challenges.prerequisites:
- Completed the EASY `BookController` pipeline challenge
- Know `@UseGuards`, `@SetMetadata`, `Reflector`
- Know `class-validator`, `ValidationPipe`, `ExceptionFilter`
challenges.description: Push the pipeline to a production-grade scenario: a CRUD Article feature with Authentication (fake-decoded token), Authorization by role, a custom Pipe for a query parameter, and an Interceptor timing every request. This challenge verifies your ability to stack guards in the correct order (JwtAuthGuard must run before RolesGuard because RolesGuard needs to read req.user), place logic in the right layer, and handle the 3 required edge cases for auth/role/validation.
challenges.requirements:
Create a ***NestJS*** project with folder name `article-auth-role-crud`. Implement 4 endpoints over mock data (in-memory array of 3 sample articles):
- `GET /articles?tag=<tag>` - list, optionally filtered by `tag`; **public** (no token required).
- `POST /articles` - create; requires authentication (any role).
- `PATCH /articles/:id` - update; requires authentication.
- `DELETE /articles/:id` - delete; only `admin` may call it.

Implement every pipeline layer (each class in a single file):

contents.title: Multi-Environment Configuration and Production-Ready Logging
contents.description: Build a multi-environment configuration system with ConfigModule, integrate Winston Logger with multiple transports, and create a professional logging pipeline ready for production.
contents.body:
## I. Introduction

Many developers building **NestJS** applications hardcode configuration values like database passwords and API keys directly in source code, and rely on `console.log` for logging. This may work locally, but in **production** it breaks down: sensitive information can leak through git, unstructured logs are hard to query in monitoring systems, and environment-specific behavior becomes difficult to manage.

This lesson solves **three core problems**: multi-environment configuration management using **ConfigModule** with **registerAs()**, replacing the default logger with **Winston** and multiple transports (Console, File, Loki), and connecting everything into a production-ready logging pipeline.

## II. Essence

This lesson follows a **code-first** approach: inspect the real bootstrap flow in source code to see how **ConfigModule** feeds settings into **WinstonModule**, then run APIs to validate environment-specific logging behavior.

Clone [here](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/system-design-mastery/introduction-to-kubernetes)

### Runtime Dependency Diagram

```mermaid
graph LR
    Env[.env.local / .env.production] --> ConfigModule[ConfigModule.forRoot]
    ConfigModule --> ConfigService[ConfigService]
    ConfigService --> WinstonFactory[getWinstonOptions]
    WinstonFactory --> WinstonModule[WinstonModule.forRootAsync]
    WinstonModule --> App[AppModule]
    App --> Main[main.ts bootstrap]
    Main --> Logger[WINSTON_MODULE_NEST_PROVIDER]
    Main --> API[GET /]
```

### Source Code Tree (File Level)

```mermaid
treeView-beta
    "src"
        "main.ts"
        "app.module.ts"
        "app.controller.ts"
        "config"
            "app.config.ts"
            "log.config.ts"
            "index.ts"
        "common"
            "logger"
                "winston.config.ts"
```

### Environment Setup and Run Flow

- **1. Prerequisites:** Require `Node.js LTS`, `npm`, and git.
- **2. Clone source demo:** Clone/pull source code for the correct context:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/fullstack-mastery/production-ready-config-and-logging
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Install dependencies:** Install packages in the project folder:
  ```bash
  npm install
  ```
- **4. Run command:** Run the app in local or production mode:
  ```bash
  npm run start:dev
  ```
  ```bash
  NODE_ENV=production npm run start:dev
  ```
- **5. Success signal:** The app starts on configured port (`app.port`), and bootstrap logs show `[Env: local|production]`.

### Application Testing

- **Step 1:** Test root endpoint `GET /` in local mode.

  **API Title:** **App API - health text - GET http://localhost:3000/**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send `GET` to `http://localhost:3000/`.

  **JSON Body:** No body for `GET`.

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3000/
  ```

  *Expected result:* API returns text from `AppService`, and Winston is used instead of Nest's default logger.

  *Conclusion:* Global logger bootstrap succeeds through `app.useLogger(winstonLogger)`.

- **Step 2:** Compare logging behavior between local and production.

  **API Title:** **Runtime config compare - local vs production - GET http://localhost:3000/**

  **How to call API:** Run the app twice with `NODE_ENV=local` and `NODE_ENV=production`, then call the same endpoint `GET /`.

  **JSON Body:** No body for `GET`.

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3000/
  ```

  **Trace code execution (by file):**
  - [`src/app.module.ts:16`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/production-ready-config-and-logging/src/app.module.ts#L16) -> `ConfigModule.forRoot()`
  - [`src/app.module.ts:26`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/production-ready-config-and-logging/src/app.module.ts#L26) -> `WinstonModule.forRootAsync()`
  - [`src/config/app.config.ts:14`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/production-ready-config-and-logging/src/config/app.config.ts#L14) -> `appConfig`
  - [`src/config/log.config.ts:10`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/production-ready-config-and-logging/src/config/log.config.ts#L10) -> `logConfig`
  - [`src/common/logger/winston.config.ts:11`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/production-ready-config-and-logging/src/common/logger/winston.config.ts#L11) -> `getWinstonOptions()`
  - [`src/main.ts:11`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/production-ready-config-and-logging/src/main.ts#L11) -> `bootstrap()`

  ```ts
  // Phase 1 - Trace paragraph 1
  // src/app.module.ts:16
  ConfigModule.forRoot({
    envFilePath: [`.env.${process.env.NODE_ENV || 'local'}`, '.env'],
    isGlobal: true,
    load: [appConfig, logConfig],
  });

  // Phase 2 - Trace paragraph 2
  // src/app.module.ts:26
  WinstonModule.forRootAsync({
    inject: [ConfigService],
    useFactory: (configService: ConfigService) => {
      const loggingSettings = configService.get('log');
      return getWinstonOptions(loggingSettings);
    },
  });

  // Phase 3 - Trace paragraph 3
  // src/main.ts:11
  const app = await NestFactory.create(AppModule, { logger: false });
  const winstonLogger = app.get(WINSTON_MODULE_NEST_PROVIDER);
  app.useLogger(winstonLogger);
  const configService = app.get(ConfigService);
  const port = configService.get<number>('app.port') || 3000;
  const nodeEnv = configService.get<string>('app.nodeEnv');
  await app.listen(port);
  winstonLogger.log({
    level: 'info',
    message: `ðŸš€ Application is running on: http://localhost:${port} [Env: ${nodeEnv}]`,
    context: 'Bootstrap',
  });
  ```

  *Expected result:* Local mode prioritizes console transport; production enables additional transports based on `logConfig` (file/Loki if configured).

  *Conclusion:* One codebase, multiple environments; logging behavior changes by `NODE_ENV` without touching business code.

## III. Core Concepts

### 1. ***Config Namespace with `registerAs()`***

- **Role:** Group environment variables under `app` / `log` namespaces instead of scattered `process.env` usage.
- **Common mistake:** Accessing env keys directly in many files without defaults/fallbacks.
- **Production impact:** Harder config control; wrong env values can trigger deployment incidents.

### 2. ***Winston Async Bootstrap***

- **Role:** Use `WinstonModule.forRootAsync()` so logger initialization happens after config is loaded.
- **Common mistake:** Hard-initializing logger before `ConfigService` is available.
- **Production impact:** Logger receives incorrect levels/transports for the environment.

### 3. ***Global Logger Override***

- **Role:** Disable default logger (`logger: false`) then set Winston with `app.useLogger(...)`.
- **Common mistake:** Running multiple loggers with different formats in parallel.
- **Production impact:** Fragmented logs, difficult querying, and weak incident correlation.

### 4. ***Transport Strategy***

- **Role:** Choose console/file/Loki by `logConfig` to balance local debugging and production observability.
- **Common mistake:** Relying only on console logs.
- **Production impact:** No centralized logs and slower incident investigation.

## IV. Advanced Techniques

A production-ready **NestJS** application requires **three pillars**: multi-environment configuration with **ConfigModule** and **registerAs()**, structured logging with **Winston** and multiple transports for centralized monitoring, and standardized response/error handling through **Interceptor** and **Exception Filter** to protect internal details.

These components do not operate independently; they are tightly connected: **ConfigService** provides settings for **WinstonModule**, Winston records logs for **ExceptionFilter**, and all behavior changes based on `NODE_ENV`.

**Conclusion:** Do not wait until production deployment to think about configuration and logging. Set them up from your first lines of code, and your application will be ready to move from dev machine to production server with one environment variable.

## V. Interview Questions

1. **Interview Question:**  
   â€œWhy does `main.ts` create the app with `logger: false` and then call `app.useLogger(winstonLogger)`?â€
   - **What is being assessed:** Understanding logger bootstrap lifecycle and logging pipeline standardization.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Avoid running default logger in parallel; ensure all logs flow through Winston with consistent format/transport.

2. **Interview Question:**  
   â€œIf `NODE_ENV=production` but the Loki host is wrong, how should logging behave so the app still runs?â€
   - **What is being assessed:** Resilience thinking for observability dependencies.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Logger should degrade gracefully (for example, fallback to console/file), keep the app alive, and emit alerts for ops handling.

3. **Interview Question:**  
   â€œHow do `ConfigModule.forRoot` + `registerAs` help when many modules share config across a team?â€
   - **What is being assessed:** Ability to organize config by namespace and reduce coupling.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Clear namespaces (`app`, `log`), avoid key collisions, reduce scattered `process.env` usage, and improve testability/extensibility.

## I. Lời mở đầu

Nhiều lập trình viên khi xây dựng ứng dụng ***NestJS*** thường hardcode các giá trị cấu hình như mật khẩu database và ***API*** key trực tiếp trong source code, đồng thời dùng `console.log` để ghi log. Cách làm này có thể hoạt động ổn trên máy local, nhưng khi lên **production** thì mọi thứ sụp đổ: thông tin nhạy cảm có thể bị lộ qua git, log không có cấu trúc rất khó truy vấn trong hệ thống monitoring, và hành vi theo từng môi trường trở nên khó quản lý.

Bài học này giải quyết **ba vấn đề cốt lõi**: quản lý cấu hình đa môi trường bằng ***ConfigModule*** với `registerAs()`, thay thế logger mặc định bằng ***Winston*** với nhiều transport (Console, File, Loki), và kết nối tất cả vào một pipeline logging sẵn sàng cho production.

## II. Bản chất

Bài này đi theo hướng **code-first**: đọc luồng bootstrap thực trong source để thấy ***ConfigModule*** nạp cấu hình vào ***WinstonModule*** như thế nào, rồi chạy ***API*** để xác nhận hành vi logging theo từng môi trường.

Clone tại [đây](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/fullstack-mastery/production-ready-config-and-logging)

### Sơ đồ phụ thuộc runtime

```mermaid
graph LR
    Env[.env.local / .env.production] --> ConfigModule[ConfigModule.forRoot]
    ConfigModule --> ConfigService[ConfigService]
    ConfigService --> WinstonFactory[getWinstonOptions]
    WinstonFactory --> WinstonModule[WinstonModule.forRootAsync]
    WinstonModule --> App[AppModule]
    App --> Main[main.ts bootstrap]
    Main --> Logger[WINSTON_MODULE_NEST_PROVIDER]
    Main --> API[GET /]
```

### Sơ đồ cây source code (file-level)

```mermaid
treeView-beta
    "src"
        "main.ts"
        "app.module.ts"
        "app.controller.ts"
        "config"
            "app.config.ts"
            "log.config.ts"
            "index.ts"
        "common"
            "logger"
                "winston.config.ts"
```

### Chuẩn bị Môi trường và Luồng Cài đặt

- **1. Prerequisites:** Cần `Node.js LTS`, `npm` và git.
- **2. Clone source demo:** Clone/pull source để đọc đúng context code:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/fullstack-mastery/production-ready-config-and-logging
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Cài dependency:** Cài package tại thư mục project:
  ```bash
  npm install
  ```
- **4. Lệnh khởi chạy:** Chạy app ở chế độ local hoặc production:
  ```bash
  npm run start:dev
  ```
  ```bash
  NODE_ENV=production npm run start:dev
  ```
- **5. Tín hiệu thành công:** App khởi động trên port đã cấu hình (`app.port`); log bootstrap hiển thị `[Env: local|production]`.

### Kiểm thử ứng dụng

- **Bước 1:** Test endpoint gốc `GET /` ở chế độ local.

  **Tiêu đề API:** **App API — health text — GET http://localhost:3000/:**

  **Hướng dẫn gọi API:** Dùng Postman gửi `GET` vào `http://localhost:3000/`.

  **Body JSON:** Không có body với request `GET`.

  Hoặc dùng **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3000/
  ```

  *Kết quả mong đợi:* ***API*** trả text từ `AppService`; ***Winston*** được sử dụng thay cho logger mặc định của ***NestJS***.

  *Kết luận:* Bootstrap logger toàn cục thành công thông qua `app.useLogger(winstonLogger)`.

- **Bước 2:** So sánh hành vi logging giữa chế độ local và production.

  **Tiêu đề API:** **Runtime config compare — local vs production — GET http://localhost:3000/:**

  **Hướng dẫn gọi API:** Chạy app hai lần với `NODE_ENV=local` và `NODE_ENV=production`, rồi gọi cùng endpoint `GET /`.

  **Body JSON:** Không có body với request `GET`.

  Hoặc dùng **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3000/
  ```

  **Trace code execution (theo file):**
  - [`src/app.module.ts:16`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/production-ready-config-and-logging/src/app.module.ts#L16) -> `ConfigModule.forRoot()`
  - [`src/app.module.ts:26`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/production-ready-config-and-logging/src/app.module.ts#L26) -> `WinstonModule.forRootAsync()`
  - [`src/config/app.config.ts:14`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/production-ready-config-and-logging/src/config/app.config.ts#L14) -> `appConfig`
  - [`src/config/log.config.ts:10`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/production-ready-config-and-logging/src/config/log.config.ts#L10) -> `logConfig`
  - [`src/common/logger/winston.config.ts:11`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/production-ready-config-and-logging/src/common/logger/winston.config.ts#L11) -> `getWinstonOptions()`
  - [`src/main.ts:11`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/production-ready-config-and-logging/src/main.ts#L11) -> `bootstrap()`

  ```ts
  // Phase 1 - ConfigModule nạp biến môi trường theo namespace
  // src/app.module.ts:16
  ConfigModule.forRoot({
    envFilePath: [`.env.${process.env.NODE_ENV || 'local'}`, '.env'],
    isGlobal: true,
    load: [appConfig, logConfig],
  });

  // Phase 2 - WinstonModule khởi tạo async dựa trên config đã nạp
  // src/app.module.ts:26
  WinstonModule.forRootAsync({
    inject: [ConfigService],
    useFactory: (configService: ConfigService) => {
      const loggingSettings = configService.get('log');
      return getWinstonOptions(loggingSettings);
    },
  });

  // Phase 3 - Bootstrap: tắt logger mặc định, thay bằng Winston
  // src/main.ts:11
  const app = await NestFactory.create(AppModule, { logger: false });
  const winstonLogger = app.get(WINSTON_MODULE_NEST_PROVIDER);
  app.useLogger(winstonLogger);
  const configService = app.get(ConfigService);
  const port = configService.get<number>('app.port') || 3000;
  const nodeEnv = configService.get<string>('app.nodeEnv');
  await app.listen(port);
  winstonLogger.log({
    level: 'info',
    message: `🚀 Application is running on: http://localhost:${port} [Env: ${nodeEnv}]`,
    context: 'Bootstrap',
  });
  ```

  *Kết quả mong đợi:* Chế độ local ưu tiên console transport; production bật thêm transport bổ sung dựa trên `logConfig` (file/Loki nếu được cấu hình).

  *Kết luận:* Một codebase, nhiều môi trường — hành vi logging thay đổi theo `NODE_ENV` mà không cần sửa business code.

## III. Các khái niệm cốt lõi

### 1. ***Config Namespace với `registerAs()`***

- **Vai trò:** Nhóm biến môi trường theo namespace `app` / `log` thay vì dùng `process.env` rải rác.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Truy cập trực tiếp env key ở nhiều file mà không có giá trị mặc định/fallback.
- **Hệ quả production:** Khó kiểm soát config; giá trị env sai có thể gây sự cố deployment.

### 2. ***Winston Async Bootstrap***

- **Vai trò:** Dùng `WinstonModule.forRootAsync()` để logger khởi tạo sau khi config đã được nạp xong.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Hard-init logger trước khi ***ConfigService*** sẵn sàng.
- **Hệ quả production:** Logger nhận sai level/transport cho môi trường đang chạy.

### 3. ***Global Logger Override***

- **Vai trò:** Tắt logger mặc định (`logger: false`) rồi gán ***Winston*** qua `app.useLogger(...)`.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Chạy song song nhiều logger với format khác nhau.
- **Hệ quả production:** Log bị phân mảnh, truy vấn khó và khả năng correlate incident yếu.

### 4. ***Transport Strategy***

- **Vai trò:** Chọn console/file/Loki theo `logConfig` để cân bằng giữa debug local và observability production.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Chỉ dựa vào console log cho toàn bộ hệ thống.
- **Hệ quả production:** Không có centralized logs, điều tra sự cố chậm hơn nhiều.

## IV. Kỹ thuật nâng cao

Ứng dụng ***NestJS*** sẵn sàng cho production đòi hỏi **ba trụ cột**: cấu hình đa môi trường với ***ConfigModule*** và `registerAs()`, logging có cấu trúc với ***Winston*** và nhiều transport để monitoring tập trung, cùng xử lý response/error chuẩn hóa qua ***Interceptor*** và ***Exception Filter*** để bảo vệ thông tin nội bộ.

Các thành phần này không hoạt động độc lập mà liên kết chặt chẽ: ***ConfigService*** cung cấp cấu hình cho ***WinstonModule***, ***Winston*** ghi log cho ***ExceptionFilter***, và toàn bộ hành vi thay đổi dựa trên `NODE_ENV`.

**Kết luận:** Đừng đợi đến khi deploy production mới nghĩ đến config và logging. Thiết lập chúng ngay từ những dòng code đầu tiên, và ứng dụng sẽ sẵn sàng chuyển từ máy dev sang production server chỉ với một biến môi trường.

## V. Các mẫu câu phỏng vấn

1. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   "Vì sao `main.ts` tạo app với `logger: false` rồi mới gọi `app.useLogger(winstonLogger)`?"
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Hiểu vòng đời bootstrap logger và chuẩn hóa pipeline logging.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Tránh chạy song song logger mặc định; đảm bảo mọi log đều đi qua ***Winston*** với format/transport nhất quán.

2. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   "Nếu `NODE_ENV=production` nhưng host Loki bị sai, hệ thống logging nên xử lý thế nào để app vẫn chạy?"
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Tư duy resilience đối với dependency observability.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Logger nên graceful degrade (fallback về console/file), giữ app sống và phát cảnh báo cho ops xử lý.

3. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   "`ConfigModule.forRoot` + `registerAs` giúp gì khi nhiều module cùng chia sẻ config trong một team?"
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Khả năng tổ chức config theo namespace và giảm coupling.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Namespace rõ ràng (`app`, `log`), tránh xung đột key, giảm `process.env` rải rác và cải thiện khả năng test/mở rộng.
Xây dựng hệ thống cấu hình đa môi trường với ConfigModule, tích hợp Winston Logger với nhiều transport, và tạo pipeline logging chuyên nghiệp sẵn sàng cho production.
Cấu hình đa môi trường và Logging chuẩn Production

challenges.title: Multi-environment configuration with 3 config namespaces and Winston structured logging for PaymentGateway
challenges.prerequisites:
- Completed the EASY cross-module DI challenge
- Basic knowledge of `@nestjs/config`, `registerAs`, `ConfigService`
- Basic knowledge of `winston` (format, transport)
- Understanding of environment variables, `process.env`, `dotenv`
challenges.description: Build a NestJS project for a PaymentGateway feature with production-ready config & logging. Configuration is split into 3 namespaces (app, database, payment), loaded by NODEENV from .env.development or .env.production, and validated against a Joi schema - a missing required variable crashes the app at startup (fail-fast), never halfway. Logging uses Winston with JSON console + file logs/app.log; every log carries level, timestamp, context.
challenges.requirements:
Create a ***NestJS*** project with folder name `payment-gateway-config-namespaces`. Implement:
- **3 namespace config files** under `src/config/`: `app.config.ts` (name, port, nodeEnv), `database.config.ts` (host, port, user, password, name), `payment.config.ts` (provider, apiKey, timeoutMs, webhookSecret). Each file exports default `registerAs('<namespace>', () => ({...}))`.
- **2 env files** at the root: `.env.development` and `.env.production`; ship `.env.example.development` + `.env.example.production` committed to the repo (the real `.env.*` files must be git-ignored). At least **3 variables must differ** between the two environments (e.g. `APP_PORT`, `DB_NAME`, `PAYMENT_PROVIDER`).
- **Joi validation schema** covering all required variables, registered via `ConfigModule.forRoot({ isGlobal: true, load: [appConfig, databaseConfig, paymentConfig], validationSchema, validationOptions: { abortEarly: true, allowUnknown: false } })`; missing a required variable -> `process.exit(1)` with a clear log naming the missing variable.
- **Winston logger** wired globally via `nest-winston`: two transports - `Console` with `json()` format and `File({ filename: 'logs/app.log' })` with `json()` format. Every log has `level`, `timestamp` (ISO), `context` (class name), `message`. Replace Nest's default logger via `app.useLogger(app.get(WINSTON_MODULE_NEST_PROVIDER))`.
- **Business feature:** `PaymentGatewayModule` with `PaymentGatewayService` exposing `charge(orderId: string, amount: number)` that injects `ConfigService`, reads `payment.apiKey` + `payment.timeoutMs`, logs `'[PaymentGateway] charging'` with context, and returns `{orderId, amount, provider, chargedAt}`. Endpoint `POST /payments/charge` accepts `{orderId, amount}` and calls the service.

**Forbidden:**
- Hardcoding any secret in code (including fake default values like `= 'sk_live_xxx'`). Fallbacks are allowed only for obvious placeholders like `'CHANGE_ME'`, or must throw when missing.
- Using `console.log` / `console.error` anywhere; logging only through Nest's `Logger` or `winston`.
- Committing real `.env.development` / `.env.production` to git.

challenges.title: Correlation-id propagation and Winston formatter masking sensitive fields for PaymentGateway
challenges.prerequisites:
- Completed the EASY challenge `0-payment-gateway-config-namespaces-easy`
- Understanding of NestJS `Middleware`
- Basic knowledge of `AsyncLocalStorage` (node:async_hooks)
- Basic knowledge of custom `winston.format`
challenges.description: Upgrade the EASY PaymentGateway app into a production-ready service with two logging capabilities that are non-negotiable in production: (1) correlation-id propagation - every log line within the same request carries the same requestId, whether the client already sent x-request-id or the server generates it; (2) a dedicated Winston formatter that masks sensitive fields (password, cardNumber, cvv, webhookSecret) into before writing - no JSON.stringify(...).replace(...) hacks. requestId propagation must work across async boundaries (Promise, setTimeout) via AsyncLocalStorage.
challenges.requirements:
Reuse the EASY codebase (or fork/clone it into a new project `correlation-id-mask-logger`). Additional requirements:
- **Correlation-id middleware** mounted globally: read the `x-request-id` header; if present **and** it matches the UUID v4 regex -> reuse it, otherwise generate a new one via `crypto.randomUUID()`. Attach `requestId` on `req` and **set it into `AsyncLocalStorage`** so it propagates across the entire request scope (including async work inside services).
- **Response header** `x-request-id` is always set on the response, with the current active value.
- **Custom Winston mask formatter** (built on `winston.format((info) => {...})`), recursively walking the whole `info` object, with keys in `['password','cardNumber','cvv','webhookSecret']` (case-insensitive) -> replace value with `'***'`. The formatter must run **before** `winston.format.json()`.
- **RequestId injector formatter:** another `winston.format((info) => {...})` that reads `requestId` from `AsyncLocalStorage` and assigns it to `info.requestId` when present; assigns nothing otherwise (logs outside the request context must still be valid).
- **Business feature:** `POST /payments/charge` accepts `{orderId, amount, card: {number, cvv}, password}` (a fake schema designed to carry sensitive fields). The service intentionally logs the raw body `this.logger.log({ message: 'charging', body }, ctx)` so we can verify masking before disk writes. `GET /payments/health` logs `requestId` twice (before/after an async boundary) to verify propagation.
- **Unit test** for the masker (`mask.formatter.spec.ts`): at least 4 cases - mask a root-level password, mask nested `card.cvv`, leave non-sensitive fields untouched, handle case-insensitivity (`Password`, `CARDNUMBER`).

**Forbidden:**
- `JSON.stringify(obj).replace(...)` or string regex as a masking strategy -> **0 on every masking prompt**.
- Storing `requestId` in a global variable, a singleton, or passing it as a parameter through services to "work around" AsyncLocalStorage.
- Hardcoding secrets or dropping any EASY rule (still 3 config namespaces, Winston console + file, fail-fast validation).

translations.value: Nâng cấp app PaymentGateway ở challenge EASY thành một dịch vụ production-ready với 2 tính năng logging bắt buộc cho môi trường thật: (1) correlation-id propagation - mọi log trong cùng 1 request đều mang chung requestId, hỗ trợ cả trường hợp client đã gửi sẵn header x-request-id lẫn trường hợp server tự sinh; (2) formatter Winston chuyên dụng mask field nhạy cảm (password, cardNumber, cvv, webhookSecret) thành trước khi ghi - không dùng thủ thuật JSON.stringify(...).replace(...). Propagate requestId phải hoạt động xuyên qua các async boundary (Promise, setTimeout) bằng AsyncLocalStorage.

- Đã xong challenge EASY `0-payment-gateway-config-namespaces-easy`
- Hiểu `Middleware` trong NestJS
- Biết cơ bản `AsyncLocalStorage` (node:async_hooks)
- Biết `winston.format` custom

Tái sử dụng codebase EASY (hoặc fork / clone về project mới tên `correlation-id-mask-logger`). Yêu cầu cộng thêm:
- **Correlation-id middleware** áp global: đọc header `x-request-id`; nếu có **và** match regex UUID v4 -> tái sử dụng, ngược lại sinh mới bằng `crypto.randomUUID()`. Gắn `requestId` vào `req` và **set vào `AsyncLocalStorage`** để propagate qua toàn request scope (bao gồm các tác vụ async bên trong service).
- **Response header** `x-request-id` luôn được set trả về client, bằng giá trị đang active.
- **Winston formatter mask** custom (là `winston.format((info) => {...})`), quét **đệ quy** toàn bộ `info` object, với key ∈ `['password','cardNumber','cvv','webhookSecret']` (case-insensitive) -> thay value thành chuỗi `'***'`. Formatter phải chạy **trước** `winston.format.json()`.
- **RequestId injector formatter:** 1 `winston.format((info) => {...})` khác đọc `requestId` từ `AsyncLocalStorage` và gán vào `info.requestId` nếu có, không gán gì nếu không có (log ngoài request context vẫn hợp lệ).
- **Feature nghiệp vụ:** endpoint `POST /payments/charge` nhận body `{orderId, amount, card: {number, cvv}, password}` (schema fake, để có field nhạy cảm). Service log toàn bộ body raw `this.logger.log({ message: 'charging', body }, ctx)` (CÓ chủ ý để test masker mask thành công trước khi ghi xuống file). Endpoint `GET /payments/health` log ra `requestId` để verify propagation.
- **Unit test** cho masker (`mask.formatter.spec.ts`): ít nhất 4 case - mask root level password, mask nested `card.cvv`, không mask field không nhạy cảm, case-insensitive (`Password`, `CARDNUMBER`).

**Cấm tuyệt đối:**
- Dùng `JSON.stringify(obj).replace(...)` hoặc regex trên string để mask -> **0 toàn prompt masking**.
- Set `requestId` qua global variable, singleton, hoặc truyền tham số xuyên các service để "work around" AsyncLocalStorage.
- Hardcode secret / xoá rule EASY (vẫn giữ 3 namespace config, Winston console + file, fail-fast).
Correlation-id propagation và Winston formatter mask sensitive field cho PaymentGateway

Upgrade the EASY PaymentGateway app into a production-ready service with two logging capabilities that are non-negotiable in production: (1) correlation-id propagation - every log line within the same request carries the same requestId, whether the client already sent x-request-id or the server generates it; (2) a dedicated Winston formatter that masks sensitive fields (password, cardNumber, cvv, webhookSecret) into before writing - no JSON.stringify(...).replace(...) hacks. requestId propagation must work across async boundaries (Promise, setTimeout) via AsyncLocalStorage.

- Completed the EASY challenge `0-payment-gateway-config-namespaces-easy`
- Understanding of NestJS `Middleware`
- Basic knowledge of `AsyncLocalStorage` (node:async_hooks)
- Basic knowledge of custom `winston.format`

Reuse the EASY codebase (or fork/clone it into a new project `correlation-id-mask-logger`). Additional requirements:
- **Correlation-id middleware** mounted globally: read the `x-request-id` header; if present **and** it matches the UUID v4 regex -> reuse it, otherwise generate a new one via `crypto.randomUUID()`. Attach `requestId` on `req` and **set it into `AsyncLocalStorage`** so it propagates across the entire request scope (including async work inside services).
- **Response header** `x-request-id` is always set on the response, with the current active value.
- **Custom Winston mask formatter** (built on `winston.format((info) => {...})`), recursively walking the whole `info` object, with keys in `['password','cardNumber','cvv','webhookSecret']` (case-insensitive) -> replace value with `'***'`. The formatter must run **before** `winston.format.json()`.
- **RequestId injector formatter:** another `winston.format((info) => {...})` that reads `requestId` from `AsyncLocalStorage` and assigns it to `info.requestId` when present; assigns nothing otherwise (logs outside the request context must still be valid).
- **Business feature:** `POST /payments/charge` accepts `{orderId, amount, card: {number, cvv}, password}` (a fake schema designed to carry sensitive fields). The service intentionally logs the raw body `this.logger.log({ message: 'charging', body }, ctx)` so we can verify masking before disk writes. `GET /payments/health` logs `requestId` twice (before/after an async boundary) to verify propagation.
- **Unit test** for the masker (`mask.formatter.spec.ts`): at least 4 cases - mask a root-level password, mask nested `card.cvv`, leave non-sensitive fields untouched, handle case-insensitivity (`Password`, `CARDNUMBER`).

- `JSON.stringify(obj).replace(...)` or string regex as a masking strategy -> **0 on every masking prompt**.
- Storing `requestId` in a global variable, a singleton, or passing it as a parameter through services to "work around" AsyncLocalStorage.
- Hardcoding secrets or dropping any EASY rule (still 3 config namespaces, Winston console + file, fail-fast validation).

contents.title: SQL and NoSQL in NestJS
contents.description: Compare the core differences between Relational (SQL) and Non-relational (NoSQL) databases to decide when to use PostgreSQL and when to use MongoDB in a NestJS project.
contents.body:
## I. Introduction

Many developers starting backend projects default to **PostgreSQL** or **MySQL** because "everyone uses them." But as systems grow, they face issues like rigid schemas that are hard to evolve quickly, or heavy **JOIN** queries that slow down APIs.

On the other hand, some teams overuse **MongoDB** for flexibility, then realize NoSQL is not a silver bullet when strict financial transaction integrity is required. This lesson helps you understand each model fundamentally so you can make decisions based on requirements, not trends.

## II. Essence

This lesson follows a **source-first** approach: inspect code comparing two data access pipelines (**TypeORM/PostgreSQL** and **Mongoose/MongoDB**) first, then call APIs to see when SQL or NoSQL is the better choice.

Clone [here](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/fullstack-mastery/sql-vs-nosql-in-nestjs)

### Runtime Dependency Diagram

```mermaid
graph LR
    Client((Client))
    Client --> CompareController[CompareController]
    CompareController --> CompareService[CompareService]
    CompareService --> SqlRepo[TypeORM Repository - PostgreSQL]
    CompareService --> NoSqlModel[Mongoose Model - MongoDB]
    SqlRepo --> PG[(PostgreSQL)]
    NoSqlModel --> MDB[(MongoDB)]
```

### Source Code Tree (File Level)

```mermaid
treeView-beta
    "src"
        "app.module.ts"
        "modules"
            "compare-db"
                "compare-db.module.ts"
                "compare-db.controller.ts"
                "compare-db.service.ts"
                "dto/compare-query.dto.ts"
            "sql"
                "entities/order.entity.ts"
                "repositories/order.repository.ts"
            "nosql"
                "schemas/activity-log.schema.ts"
                "models/activity-log.model.ts"
```

### Environment Setup and Run Flow

- **1. Prerequisites:** Require `Node.js LTS`, `npm`, Docker Desktop, and git.
- **2. Clone source demo:** Clone/pull source code to match the correct context:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/fullstack-mastery/sql-vs-nosql-in-nestjs
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Start data infrastructure:** Run PostgreSQL and MongoDB with docker compose:
  ```bash
  docker compose up -d
  ```
- **4. Install dependencies and run app:** Install packages and start the NestJS server:
  ```bash
  npm install
  npm run start:dev
  ```
- **5. Success signal:** App runs on port `3000`; compare endpoint returns payload with both `sqlResult` and `noSqlResult`.

### Application Testing

- **Step 1:** Check compare endpoint for read-oriented use case.

  **API Title:** **Compare DB API - SQL vs NoSQL recommendation - GET http://localhost:3000/compare-db?useCase=order-history**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send `GET` to `http://localhost:3000/compare-db?useCase=order-history`.

  **JSON Body:** No body for `GET`.

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl "http://localhost:3000/compare-db?useCase=order-history"
  ```

  **Trace code execution (by file):**
  - [`src/modules/compare-db/compare-db.controller.ts:22`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/sql-vs-nosql-in-nestjs/src/modules/compare-db/compare-db.controller.ts#L22) -> `CompareDbController.compare()`
  - [`src/modules/compare-db/compare-db.service.ts:31`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/sql-vs-nosql-in-nestjs/src/modules/compare-db/compare-db.service.ts#L31) -> `CompareDbService.recommendStorage()`
  - [`src/modules/sql/repositories/order.repository.ts:18`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/sql-vs-nosql-in-nestjs/src/modules/sql/repositories/order.repository.ts#L18) -> `OrderRepository.findOrderHistory()`
  - [`src/modules/nosql/models/activity-log.model.ts:14`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/sql-vs-nosql-in-nestjs/src/modules/nosql/models/activity-log.model.ts#L14) -> `ActivityLogModel.findRecentEvents()`

- **Step 2:** Check endpoint for flexible logging use case.

  **API Title:** **Compare DB API - flexible log use case - GET http://localhost:3000/compare-db?useCase=tracking-log**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send `GET` to `http://localhost:3000/compare-db?useCase=tracking-log`.

  **JSON Body:** No body for `GET`.

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl "http://localhost:3000/compare-db?useCase=tracking-log"
  ```

  *Expected result:* Strict relational use cases favor SQL; rapidly changing data use cases favor NoSQL.

  *Conclusion:* SQL/NoSQL decisions must come from data models and consistency needs, not hype.

## III. Core Concepts

### 1. ***ACID and Transactional Data***

- **Role:** SQL (PostgreSQL) ensures integrity for finance, orders, and wallet use cases.
- **Common mistake:** Using NoSQL for multi-table transactional needs without clear compensation strategies.
- **Production impact:** Balance inconsistencies, invalid order states, and hard auditing.

### 2. ***Flexible Schema and Change Velocity***

- **Role:** NoSQL (MongoDB) fits logs, events, and metadata that change continuously.
- **Common mistake:** Forcing high-volatility data into rigid relational schemas from day one.
- **Production impact:** Frequent migrations, high schema-change cost, and slower feature delivery.

### 3. ***Relational Queries vs Embedding***

- **Role:** SQL is strong for complex JOINs; NoSQL is strong for document embedding and fast aggregate reads.
- **Common mistake:** Modeling heavily cross-related data in MongoDB without duplication controls.
- **Production impact:** Hard query optimization, redundant data, and synchronization challenges.

### 4. ***Polyglot Persistence***

- **Role:** Combine SQL + NoSQL by bounded context to leverage the strengths of each.
- **Common mistake:** Forcing the entire system onto one DB engine.
- **Production impact:** Some use cases become tool-mismatched, causing imbalance between speed and reliability.

## IV. Advanced Techniques

In real systems, SQL vs NoSQL is not an either/or decision. A scalable architecture often uses **Polyglot Persistence**: PostgreSQL for critical transactional domains and MongoDB for flexible, high-volume event/log domains.

In NestJS, keep this manageable by clearly separating domain boundaries, exposing stable service contracts, and synchronizing cross-store data with patterns like outbox/events. This gives you flexibility without losing control over consistency and operations.

## V. Interview Questions

1. **Interview Question:**  
   “Would you choose PostgreSQL or MongoDB for an e-wallet with dense transaction history, and why?”
   - **What is being assessed:** Ability to map business requirements to ACID and consistency guarantees.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Choose PostgreSQL for primary ledger/transactions; optionally use MongoDB for supporting audit/log data.

2. **Interview Question:**  
   “When product schema changes weekly, what is the biggest risk of staying purely SQL?”
   - **What is being assessed:** Migration cost awareness and development velocity thinking.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Frequent migrations slow delivery; propose moving highly flexible data to NoSQL.

3. **Interview Question:**  
   “How should Polyglot Persistence be applied in NestJS to avoid excessive complexity?”
   - **What is being assessed:** Domain separation, coupling control, and operational observability.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Define clear SQL/NoSQL contexts, standardize service contracts, and monitor data sync with event or outbox patterns.

SQL và NoSQL trong NestJS
So sánh sự khác biệt cốt lõi giữa cơ sở dữ liệu Quan hệ (SQL) và Phi quan hệ (NoSQL), từ đó xác định khi nào nên dùng PostgreSQL, khi nào nên dùng MongoDB trong một dự án NestJS.

## I. Lời mở đầu

Nhiều lập trình viên khi bắt đầu dự án Backend thường mặc định chọn **PostgreSQL** hoặc **MySQL** vì "ai cũng dùng thế". Nhưng khi hệ thống lớn dần, họ gặp phải những vấn đề như schema cứng nhắc không thể thay đổi nhanh, hoặc những truy vấn **JOIN** chồng chất làm chậm toàn bộ API.

Ngược lại, nhóm khác lại "cuồng" **MongoDB** vì sự tự do, để rồi khi cần đảm bảo tính toàn vẹn dữ liệu giao dịch tài chính, họ mới nhận ra NoSQL không phải viên đạn bạc. Bài học này sẽ giúp bạn hiểu bản chất của từng loại, để đưa ra quyết định đúng đắn thay vì chọn theo phong trào.

## II. Bản chất

Bài này đi theo hướng **source-first**: đọc code so sánh hai pipeline truy cập dữ liệu (**TypeORM/PostgreSQL** và **Mongoose/MongoDB**) trước, sau đó gọi API để thấy rõ khi nào nên chọn SQL và khi nào nên chọn NoSQL.

Clone tại [đây](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/fullstack-mastery/sql-vs-nosql-in-nestjs)

### Sơ đồ phụ thuộc runtime

```mermaid
graph LR
    Client((Client))
    Client --> CompareController[CompareController]
    CompareController --> CompareService[CompareService]
    CompareService --> SqlRepo[TypeORM Repository - PostgreSQL]
    CompareService --> NoSqlModel[Mongoose Model - MongoDB]
    SqlRepo --> PG[(PostgreSQL)]
    NoSqlModel --> MDB[(MongoDB)]
```

### Sơ đồ cây source code (file-level)

```mermaid
treeView-beta
    "src"
        "app.module.ts"
        "modules"
            "compare-db"
                "compare-db.module.ts"
                "compare-db.controller.ts"
                "compare-db.service.ts"
                "dto/compare-query.dto.ts"
            "sql"
                "entities/order.entity.ts"
                "repositories/order.repository.ts"
            "nosql"
                "schemas/activity-log.schema.ts"
                "models/activity-log.model.ts"
```

### Chuẩn bị Môi trường và Luồng Cài đặt

- **1. Prerequisites:** Cần có `Node.js LTS`, `npm`, Docker Desktop và git.
- **2. Clone source demo:** Clone/pull source để đọc đúng context code:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/fullstack-mastery/sql-vs-nosql-in-nestjs

  ```
- **3. Khởi động hạ tầng dữ liệu:** Chạy PostgreSQL và MongoDB bằng docker compose:
  ```bash
  docker compose up -d
  ```
- **4. Cài dependency và chạy app:** Cài package rồi khởi động server NestJS:
